references.text: Stoning as a penalty for idolatry is also prescribed in Leviticus, where anyone who gives their offspring to Molech shall be stoned.
The instruction to bring the sinner outside the camp and stone them follows the same pattern as in Deuteronomy.
Stoning as a penalty for those who lead others into idolatry, with the same procedure described.
Stoning at the city gate as an execution method for serious violations of the covenant.
Both the man and the woman shall be brought to the city gate and stoned for their sin.
Achan was stoned for his sin, an example of the application of this law concerning the death penalty.
Naboth was falsely accused and led out of the city to be stoned, showing the abuse of this legal process.
The Pharisees refer to the Mosaic Law on stoning, which includes this text in Deuteronomy.
Stephen was brought outside the city and stoned, following the procedure described in the Mosaic Law.
